rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 6 (score 937.1, best so far) finished 60/60 across oval, s-bend and slalom, with slalom at 20/20 finishes, up from 11/20 at iteration 5. Iteration 7 moved the sensor lead from y=0.06 to y=0.07 and raised kd from 1.0 to 1.1 together. Its score fell to 930.9. On slalom, line-loss events rose from 0.65 to 0.95, max_error from 0.021 to 0.026, and steering_oscillation from 0.33 to 0.34. Those changes were confounded, but the net effect was negative, so the 0.07 lead is rejected. Mass is already at its 0.40 kg floor, kp 6 collapsed the oval and s-bend in iteration 4, and body_width cannot change the off-track limit because the 0.06 m floor binds.

Change. I revert the sensor lead to y=0.06, which is the iteration 6 geometry. I lower kd from 1.0 to 0.9, a single-variable test of the damping direction at the known-good lead. Everything else is the iteration 6 design: five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03 m in 15 mm steps, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], kp 4.0, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.5, line_loss last_direction.

Expected result. Oval and s-bend stay at 100% completion. Slalom line-loss events should stay near 0.65 or fall slightly. Steering_oscillation should stay at or below about 0.33. If slalom max_error or oscillation worsens, or if completion drops, the fallback is the exact iteration 6 design with kd 1.0, which is already known to score 937.1.

Hypotheses. (a) kd 0.9 does not add jitter at lead y=0.06, because the iteration 7 oscillation rise was probably caused by the larger lead. (b) Slightly less derivative damping reduces the extra lag that causes slalom line loss. (c) Completion stays at 100% on all three development tracks.

Measurements wanted. Per-track completion, max_error, line_loss_events and completion_time on slalom, plus steering_oscillation on all tracks. These will show whether kd is the driver of any change in slalom line loss.
